paper_summary: Matrix-less (binderless) syntactic foam was produced by spark plasma sintering fly-ash cenospheres (fractions 63-150 um and 150-250 um) in 20, 30 and 50 mm graphite dies at 1050-1300 C under ~0.6 kN (1.9 MPa in the 20 mm die). Sintering shrinkage starts near 900 C; apparent density rises with sintering temperature (e.g. 0.97 -> 2.3 g/cm3 for CS 63-150 um in a 20 mm die between 1050 and 1300 C) while total porosity falls from 61.5 % to 3.9 % (1050-1250 C). Compressive strength of the CS 63-150 um / 20 mm die series rises from 11 MPa to 312 MPa over 1050-1300 C, following the Rice porosity model with an extrapolated fully dense strength of 411.1 MPa.

extraction_notes: Matrix-less syntactic foam: cenospheres are sintered directly to each other with no matrix, so matrix_class is set to 'other' with matrix_name explaining there is no matrix, and particle_weight_fraction = 1.0 (the material is 100 wt% cenospheres, stated as 'matrix-less SF foam containing CS only'). process_route 'powder_metallurgy' is used for spark plasma sintering (Dr. Sinter SPS825, ~0.6 kN = 1.9 MPa in the 20 mm die, 6 Pa vacuum). cure_or_process_temperature_c holds the sintering temperature. Almost all numeric data in this paper are only in figures (Figs. 2-20); the only values stated numerically in text are the abstract/conclusions endpoints, so records exist only for the lowest and highest sintering temperature of each series and intermediate points were left out rather than read off plots. Total porosity (61.5 % at 1050 C down to 3.9 % at 1250 C) and open porosity (0.28-43 %) are the porosity of the whole matrix-less foam (inter-particle plus intra-cenosphere void), not unintended matrix porosity, so they are recorded in microstructure_notes rather than in matrix_porosity_fraction. Pre-sintering cenosphere breakage: 3 % in the 50 mm die is unambiguous and recorded; the 20 mm die CS 63-150 um numbers ('21 % and 20 %, respectively') and the CS 150-250 um numbers (23 % plus an additional 37 %) are ambiguous/cumulative and are only described in notes. Compressive strength test temperature is not stated (assumed ambient but left null); no strain rate, modulus or strain data are reported. The chemical composition table (Table 1) is a literature compilation, not measurements of these cenospheres, so no record was made from it.
